newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU seeks action on corruption.
newsitem.headline: EU seeks action on corruption.

text.p: The European Union should agree to criminalise bribery of foreign officials by EU businesses and corruption in the private sector, the European Commission said on Wednesday.

A commission policy document on fighting corruption, drawn up by the EU's Justice Commissioner Anita Gradin, also proposes getting rid at EU level of tax deductibility for bribes, which is already banned in the United States and Japan.
"Corruption is a danger to democracy and the rule of law. It distorts competition on the (EU) internal market and international trade," Gradin said in a statement.

All of the 15 EU member states already criminalise corruption involving their own officials acting at home, but legal gaps appear when the corruption takes place across the EU's borders or in the private sector.

The EU executive, seeking to launch discussions with EU governments on the problem, said it also wants in cooperation with the OECD and the World Trade Organisation to draw up tighter rules worldwide for public procurement and at an EU level to create blacklists of companies and people found to be involved in corruption.
The Commission said in a statement that its document only covered areas where policies at national level required additional EU action.
